thinking_text:
**Evaluating mirror operation**

I’m working with a mirror via the ZX plane, defining the normal at the Y midpoint between two planes, 24 Y15 and 25 Y0. I need to identify the midplane and derive the footprint and depth. I'll sketch the bottom face, perhaps projecting or mirroring the footprint. The operation involves cutting from the bottom inward, validating symmetry, and ensuring the footprint has enough clearance. Finally, I’ll extrude it 1mm in the +Y direction to complete the shape.

operations_plan.summary: Create a bottom-side lowered rounded-rectangular plateau by mirroring the existing top handle recess across the ZX midplane, restoring symmetry of the unlabeled base wrench about that plane.

steps.description: Identify the nominal top and bottom handle planes from broad skin faces 24 and 25. Face 24 is at Y=15 mm and face 25 is at Y=0 mm, so construct the ZX symmetry datum halfway between them at Y=7.5 mm. Confirm that the existing top recess floor, face 1, is at Y=14 mm and therefore has a depth of 1 mm from the top skin.

Recover the complete rounded-rectangular footprint of the existing top recess from its planar end walls, longitudinal sidewalls, and four cylindrical corner walls. Use faces 0 through 8 as the authoritative recess boundary so its length, width, position, and corner radii are preserved exactly. If feature history is available, select the existing recessed-panel cut directly; otherwise project the top opening boundary into an XZ sketch and constrain the reconstructed profile coincident with the extracted edges.

Mirror the recovered recess profile or the existing subtractive pocket feature across the ZX datum at Y=7.5 mm. Place the mirrored footprint on bottom face 25 with identical XZ coordinates, dimensions, and rounded-corner treatment. The resulting bottom plateau must be directly opposite and congruent with the existing top plateau.

Pocket-cut the mirrored rounded-rectangular profile from bottom face 25 in the +Y direction by exactly 1 mm. This creates a new bottom recess floor at Y=1 mm, which is the mirror of the top recess floor at Y=14 mm. Keep the cut confined to the straight central handle and retain the surrounding bottom perimeter frame and nominal 15 mm overall thickness.

Regenerate the solid and verify that the top and bottom plateau footprints, depths, corner radii, and longitudinal positions are mirror-equivalent about Y=7.5 mm. Confirm that the cut does not intersect the open-jaw head, ring head, ring bore, handle sidewalls, or either transition region. Treat the new bottom plateau as a new recessed-panel feature within section_handle; do not create a separate solid or alter the external planform.

operations_plan.summary: Add centered raised text reading "TOP" to the existing top lowered plateau, using Arial at 10 mm text height and a 1 mm emboss height while keeping the complete label within the plateau and below or flush with the surrounding top surface.

steps.description: Select the existing top plateau floor, planar face 1 at Y=14 mm, as the text sketch support. Extract the usable interior boundary from the recess walls represented by faces 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8. Determine the plateau center from the centroid or bounding-box center of this rounded-rectangular boundary rather than from the entire wrench.

Create a planar text sketch on face 1 with the literal content "TOP", font family Arial, and nominal character height 10 mm. Orient the word along the handle's longitudinal Z direction so the character height spans the handle width and the word length follows the elongated plateau. Center the text outline approximately at the plateau center. If the CAD system defines font height through an em-box rather than visible capital height, scale the generated outlines so the modeled text-height parameter is 10 mm while preserving the Arial proportions.

Convert the Arial text into closed sketch contours and check its full outline against the plateau boundary. Translate the text slightly about the plateau center if required so every letter, including curved portions of the O and all stroke extremities, remains strictly inside the lowered plateau with positive clearance from its straight walls and rounded corners. Do not clip, wrap, or allow the text footprint to overlap the surrounding unrecessed top skin.

Extrude the closed text contours additively from the top plateau floor in the +Y direction by exactly 1 mm and boolean-union the emboss with solid 0. Because the floor is at Y=14 mm, the embossed letter tops terminate at Y=15 mm, flush with and not above the surrounding top skin face 24. Keep the emboss as a new top-label feature associated with section_handle and do not mirror it to the bottom, since its purpose is to distinguish the top side.

Validate the completed model: confirm the text reads exactly "TOP", uses Arial geometry, has 10 mm text height and 1 mm emboss height, is approximately centered, and remains entirely within the top plateau footprint. Confirm the emboss is joined to the wrench, does not rise above Y=15 mm, and does not modify the plateau walls. Finally verify that the paired plateau geometry remains symmetric about the ZX plane when the intentionally top-only identifying text is excluded, and that the jaw opening, ring bore, wrench outline, transitions, and nominal outer thickness remain unchanged.
